# superset_database_upload (Resource)

Loads a CSV, Excel or columnar file into a table of a database connection through the upload endpoint of Superset 4.1 and later, which also creates a dataset for the table, for example to publish reference data next to the dashboards that use it. The connection must allow file uploads and list the schema in `schemas_allowed_for_file_upload` of its extra. The file is uploaded when the resource is created and whenever the content, the reading options, `already_exists` or `triggers` change; a file given by path is read at apply time, so pair it with a trigger such as `filemd5()` to upload it again when it changes. A table that disappears is uploaded again. Destroying the resource leaves the table and its dataset unless `drop_on_destroy` is set.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A connection that allows uploads into the public schema.
resource "superset_database" "warehouse" {
  connection_name   = "Warehouse"
  sqlalchemy_uri    = var.warehouse_uri
  expose_in_sqllab  = true
  allow_dml         = true
  allow_run_async   = false
  allow_file_upload = true
  extra = jsonencode({
    schemas_allowed_for_file_upload = ["public"]
  })
}

# Reference data kept next to the dashboards, uploaded again whenever the file changes.
resource "superset_database_upload" "regions" {
  database_name = superset_database.warehouse.connection_name
  table_name    = "regions"
  schema        = "public"
  file          = "${path.module}/regions.csv"
  column_dates  = ["valid_from"]
  triggers = {
    hash = filemd5("${path.module}/regions.csv")
  }
  drop_on_destroy = true
}

# A small table written in the configuration.
resource "superset_database_upload" "currencies" {
  database_name  = superset_database.warehouse.connection_name
  table_name     = "currencies"
  schema         = "public"
  content        = <<-CSV
    code,name
    EUR,Euro
    USD,US dollar
  CSV
  already_exists = "replace"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `table_name` (String) Name of the table the file is loaded into.

### Optional

- `already_exists` (String) What to do when the table exists: `replace` it, `append` the rows to it, or `fail`. Defaults to `replace`, which keeps every upload idempotent; with `fail`, a second upload of the resource fails.
- `column_data_types` (String) JSON object with the type of columns that must not be inferred, for example `{"zip": "str"}`.
- `column_dates` (List of String) Names of the columns to parse as dates.
- `columns_read` (List of String) Names of the columns to read; all of them when unset.
- `content` (String) Content of the file, for a CSV written in the configuration. Exactly one of `file` and `content` must be set.
- `database_id` (Number) Numeric identifier of the connection, looked up from `database_name` when that is set.
- `database_name` (String) Name of the database connection. Exactly one of `database_name` and `database_id` must be set.
- `dataframe_index` (Boolean) Whether the index of the data frame is written as a column.
- `day_first` (Boolean) Whether dates start with the day, as in `31/12/2026`.
- `decimal_character` (String) Decimal separator of the numbers. Defaults to a point.
- `delimiter` (String) Delimiter of a CSV file. Defaults to a comma.
- `drop_on_destroy` (Boolean) Whether the destroy drops the table through SQL Lab, which needs `allow_dml` on the connection, and deletes the dataset Superset created for it. Defaults to `false`: the table and the dataset stay.
- `file` (String) Path of the file to upload. Exactly one of `file` and `content` must be set.
- `header_row` (Number) Row of the column names, counted from 0. Defaults to the first row.
- `index_column` (String) Column to use as the index of the data frame.
- `index_label` (String) Name of the index column when it is written.
- `null_values` (List of String) Values to read as null, in addition to the defaults of pandas.
- `rows_to_read` (Number) Number of rows to read; all of them when unset.
- `schema` (String) Schema of the table. When unset, the default schema of the connection is used and only the existence of the connection is checked, not the table.
- `sheet_name` (String) Sheet of an Excel file to read. Defaults to the first one.
- `skip_blank_lines` (Boolean) Whether blank lines are skipped instead of read as rows of nulls.
- `skip_initial_space` (Boolean) Whether spaces after the delimiter are skipped.
- `skip_rows` (Number) Number of rows to skip at the start of the file.
- `triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary values whose change uploads the file again, for example `filemd5()` of the file.
- `type` (String) Kind of file: `csv`, `excel` or `columnar` (Parquet). Defaults to `csv`.

### Read-Only

- `dataset_id` (Number) Identifier of the dataset Superset created for the table; null when none was found.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the resource: the connection, the schema and the table.
